<idea-plugin>
    <id>com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt</id>
    <name>Advanced Android Project Tree</name>
    <vendor url="https://z8dn.github.io/">Zayden</vendor>

    <depends>com.intellij.modules.platform</depends>
    <depends>com.intellij.java</depends>
    <depends>org.jetbrains.plugins.gradle</depends>
    <depends>org.jetbrains.android</depends>

    <resource-bundle>messages.AndroidViewBundle</resource-bundle>

    <extensions defaultExtensionNs="com.intellij">
        <!-- Android View Settings Service -->
        <applicationService serviceImplementation="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.settings.AndroidViewSettings"/>

        <!-- Android View Settings Configurable -->
        <applicationConfigurable
                parentId="tools"
                instance="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.settings.AndroidViewSettingsConfigurable"
                id="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.settings"
                key="settings.DisplayName.text"
                bundle="messages.AndroidViewBundle"/>

        <!-- Startup Activity to refresh view on project open -->
        <postStartupActivity implementation="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.AndroidViewStartupActivity"/>

        <!-- Tree Structure Provider for adding project files to non-Android modules -->
        <treeStructureProvider implementation="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.providers.CustomNonAndroidNodeProvider"/>

        <!-- Tree Structure Provider for adding top-level ProjectFileGroupNode -->
        <treeStructureProvider implementation="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.providers.ProjectFilesTreeStructureProvider"/>

        <!-- Zoo Scopes: Makes scopes available in ScopeChooserCombo -->
        <searchScopesProvider implementation="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.scopes.ProjectFileGroupScopeProvider"/>
    </extensions>

    <!-- Android View Node Providers -->
    <extensions defaultExtensionNs="com.android.tools.idea.navigator">
        <!-- Provider that handles build directories and project files -->
        <androidViewNodeProvider implementation="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.providers.AdvancedAndroidViewProvider"/>
    </extensions>

    <!-- Toggle Actions for Android View -->
    <actions>
        <group id="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.IncludeDirectoryGroup"
               class="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.actions.IncludeDirectoryInGroupActionGroup"
               popup="true">
            <add-to-group group-id="ProjectViewPopupMenu" anchor="last"/>
        </group>
        <group id="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.AppearanceActions">
            <add-to-group group-id="ProjectView.ToolWindow.Appearance.Actions"
                          relative-to-action="ShowBuildFilesInModuleAction"
                          anchor="after"/>
            <separator/>
            <action id="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.ShowBuildDirectoryAction"
                    class="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.actions.ShowBuildDirectoryAction"/>
            <action id="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.ShowProjectFilesInModuleAction"
                    class="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.actions.ShowProjectFilesInModuleAction"/>
            <action id="CustomizeAndroidTreeViewAction"
                    class="com.z8dn.plugins.a2pt.actions.CustomizeAndroidTreeViewAction"/>
        </group>
    </actions>
</idea-plugin>

Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me compile a comprehensive, user-friendly changelog summary.

## User-Friendly Changelog for v0.0.9

Based on my analysis of the git history and code changes between v0.0.8 and HEAD, here's a concise summary of each change suitable for a user-facing changelog:

---

### **PR #52: Exclusion Patterns and Path-Based Glob Matching**

**What it does:** You can now use the `!` prefix to exclude files from file groups. For example, if you have a group with patterns `*.md` and `!archive/*.md`, it will show all Markdown files except those in the archive directory. Additionally, patterns containing `/` (like `docs/*.md`) are now matched against file paths relative to the project root, not just filenames.

**Problem solved:** Users previously couldn't exclude specific files or folders, and couldn't organize file groups by directory structure.

**Technical note:** Centralized matching logic and validates that groups have at least one inclusion pattern.

---

### **PR #53: Extended Path Filtering to Non-Module Folders**

**What it does:** Path-based patterns now work for any folder under your project root, not just Gradle modules. So if you have a top-level `docs/` or `config/` folder that isn't a Gradle module, you can create groups for files in those directories using patterns like `docs/guide.md`.

**Problem solved:** Users with non-Gradle project files (like documentation) couldn't organize them with file groups.

**Technical note:** Added dedicated scanning for path-based patterns, separate from module content-root scanning.

---

### **PR #54: Right-Click Menu for Directory Include/Exclude**

**What it does:** Right-click on any directory in the Android Project View to see two new context menu options:
- **"Include Directory in File Group"** → Shows all existing groups plus "New Group..." to create one
- **"Exclude Directory from File Group"** → Shows all existing groups to add exclusion patterns

The plugin automatically generates the correct pattern (e.g., `docs/**` for inclusion or `!docs/**` for exclusion).

**Problem solved:** Users no longer need to manually type out directory patterns in the settings dialog.

---

### **PR #55: Internationalization of UI Strings**

**What it does:** All user-visible text in the plugin (menu items, dialog labels, help text, validation messages) is now externalized to a resource bundle, making the plugin ready for translation.

**Problem solved:** Hardcoded strings prevented localization and made maintenance harder.

---

### **PR #50: IntelliJ Platform Plugin Bump**

**What it does:** Updated the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin from v2.10.5 to v2.14.0 and Gradle from 8.14.3 to 9.4.1. Also standardized build configuration naming conventions (camelCase for versions, kebab-case for library aliases).

**Problem solved:** Keeps the build system current and aligned with official IntelliJ plugin templates.

---

### **PR #51: Upgrade Target Platform to IntelliJ 2026.1**

**What it does:** Updated the plugin's minimum supported IDE version from build 252 to 261, and targets IntelliJ 2026.1 (Quail 1), which includes the latest Android Studio version.

**Problem solved:** Users on newer IDE versions can now use the latest features and bug fixes.

---

### **Buildkite CI Migration**

**What it does:** Migrated continuous integration from GitHub Actions to Buildkite with four pipeline files:
- `build.yml` - Main build, test, verify, and draft release pipeline
- `release.yml` - Publishes to JetBrains Marketplace
- `run-ui-tests.yml` - Manual UI test matrix
- `qodana_code_quality.yml` - Code quality scanning

The migration includes optimizations for CI agents (OOM fixes, Docker compatibility, Gradle 9 support).

**Problem solved:** Buildkite provides better resource management and more flexible pipeline customization than GitHub Actions for this project's needs.

---

### **Summary**

v0.0.9 focuses on **pattern flexibility** (exclusions and paths), **user convenience** (right-click menus), **localization** (i18n), and **infrastructure** (modern dependencies and CI/CD improvements). These changes make file grouping more powerful and accessible while ensuring the plugin supports the latest IDE versions.

Yep, exactly as expected. Here's how it works:

1. At build time, the [Gradle Changelog Plugin](https://github.com/JetBrains/gradle-changelog-plugin) reads `CHANGELOG.md` and looks for a section matching `pluginVersion` (currently `0.0.9`)
2. It renders that section as **HTML** (`Changelog.OutputType.HTML`)
3. That HTML becomes the `changeNotes` field embedded in the plugin descriptor
4. JetBrains Marketplace displays it as the **"What's New"** tab on your plugin page

The new format (`### Added / Fixed / Changed` subheadings + plain English descriptions) will render nicely — the subheadings become `<h3>` tags and the bullet points become `<ul><li>` lists. Much better than the old PR-title dump.

One thing worth knowing: `.withEmptySections(false)` is already set, so if a subheading has no entries it gets skipped automatically — no need to worry about leaving placeholder sections in future releases.

Yes — the CI manages `CHANGELOG.md` during the release. Here's the actual flow:

**`pipeline.yml` (runs on `main`):**
- Reads `[Unreleased]` from `CHANGELOG.md` via `gradle getChangelog --unreleased`
- Creates a **GitHub release draft** with that content

**`pipeline.release.yml` (runs on a git tag):**
- Reads the **GitHub release draft body** (which you can edit manually on GitHub)
- Runs `gradle patchChangelog --release-note="$CHANGELOG"` — this writes the release body back into `CHANGELOG.md` under the versioned section
- Publishes the plugin, then opens a PR with the patched `CHANGELOG.md`

So the intended workflow is:
1. Accumulate changes in `## [Unreleased]` as you develop
2. Merge to `main` → CI auto-creates a GitHub release draft from `[Unreleased]`
3. Edit the draft body on GitHub to polish the What's New text
4. Push a tag → CI patches `CHANGELOG.md`, publishes plugin, opens PR

**The problem with what we did:** we wrote directly into `[0.0.9]` — that section will be overwritten by `patchChangelog` when the release runs. The right place for our improved descriptions is `[Unreleased]`, so CI picks them up for the draft.

# Advanced Android Project Tree Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- File group patterns now support `!pattern` exclusion syntax — use `!*.generated.kt` to exclude files by name or `!docs/*.md` for path-relative globs ([#52](https://github.com/z8dn/advanced-android-project-view/pull/52))
- Exclusion and path-based patterns now work in non-Gradle project folders (e.g. a top-level `docs/` or `config/` directory), not only inside Gradle modules ([#53](https://github.com/z8dn/advanced-android-project-view/pull/53))
- Right-click any directory in the project tree to instantly add or exclude it from a file group — patterns are generated automatically ([#54](https://github.com/z8dn/advanced-android-project-view/pull/54))

### Changed

- Minimum supported IDE build bumped to 261 (Android Studio Quail / 2026.1) ([#51](https://github.com/z8dn/advanced-android-project-view/pull/51))
